paragraphs: At the beginning of Midrash Tehillim 91, he reports in the name of Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Simon. The statement also appears in Bamidbar Rabbah 12:3.

notes.text: The second work’s specific identity under מ״ר remains unresolved. A bounded candidate lookup in Bamidbar Rabbah2:3 did not establish the named Prozdak passage. The locator is2:3, not a chapter range.

The connected passage in saved Torat Emet Bamidbar Rabbah 12:3 names Prozdak bar Nachsha reporting Rabbi Yehudah bar Rabbi Simon. This supplies a parallel alongside the source’s מ״ר 2:3, not proof that a yod was lost in printing. The saved OYW Midrash Tehillim 91 scalar names Yehudah bar Rabbi Simon but does not include Prozdak in that selected paragraph. The source’s shorter name and both locations remain distinct.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1032) cites chapter 12, section 3 (מ״ר פ״יב־ג), where the supplied text has 2:3. In the consulted Bamidbar Rabbah 12:3, Prozdak bar Nachsha speaks in the name of Rabbi Yehudah bar Rabbi Simon about the shelter made by Betzalel. The Cambridge-based digital transcription of Midrash Tehillim 91 has Prozdaki bar Nachsha in the corresponding episode and reports the spelling Prozdak in Buber. The earlier consulted OYW paragraph gives Rabbi Yehudah bar Rabbi Simon without naming Prozdak in that paragraph.
